Features / Captures

Captures.

Screenshots, scrolling captures, screen recordings and text from the screen, with an editor built in.

S27 features

Everything in Captures.

Every feature, with its key and where it lives in Pilot.

Captures
Uncrop

Drag a crop edge past the capture and the screen round it comes back; Whole capture and As taken put it back.

Capture editor

Marks on the backdrop

Text, arrows and boxes on the backdrop as well as the capture; they stay put when an uncrop grows it.

Capture editor (B)

Snap and guides

Crop and boxes snap to the windows and edges in the capture, with guides as you move a mark.

Capture editor

Magnifier, bent arrows, smooth pen

A round lens that enlarges a detail, moved off as a callout; arrows bent by their middle; a pen that smooths a shaky line; pixelate that reads nothing under it.

Capture editor

Capture looks and sizes

Looks for the backdrop, a balance setting, sizes for each place you post (1080 × 1350 and more), and Add a capture to join two.

Capture editor (B)

Cut and speed parts

Split a recording, cut parts out and play others at ½× to 8×; the still parts found for you; blur part of the screen for a time.

Video editor

Pilot draws the pointer

Recordings keep the pointer out of the picture and the editor draws it: smooth, bigger, hidden when still, with a click ring.

Video editor

Vertical and square

Export 1080 × 1920 or 1080 × 1080 with the pointer kept in frame, motion blur on zooms, and a saved look for every recording.

Video editor

ScreenshotsHyper+S

Capture an area, a window without its shadow, or the whole screen; a thumbnail opens the editor. Each capture key captures at once: an area when you let go of the drag, a window on the click, the screen straight away. Capture tool opens the capture box instead: its bar sits under the area you drag, a click or one letter switches between Area, Window, Full screen, Scroll, Record and Text, the area keeps its handles until you press Return, and the button says what Return does.

Hyper+S an area, Hyper+Shift+S a window; Hyper+Space (Capture menu); Hyper+A the screen in Complex; Hyper+Ctrl+S Capture tool

Capture editor

Arrows, boxes, text, pen, highlighter, blur, numbered steps, crop, spotlight, colour picker and a pixel ruler.

Opens after a capture; Hyper+Space; Hyper+Shift+E opens the last one in Complex

Backdrops

Put a capture on a gradient, your wallpaper, a blur of it or a colour, with padding, shadow, corners and a ratio; save presets. Copy, save and drag include it.

Capture editor (B)

Scrolling capture

A page taller than the screen in one image; Pilot scrolls for you, up or down.

Hyper+Space; Hyper+Z in Complex; S in the capture box

Text from screen

Drag over any area and its text is copied; in the capture box, adjust the area and press Return.

Hyper+Space; Hyper+Shift+X in Complex; O in the capture box

Repeat and delay

Capture the last area again, or count down first so an open menu is in the shot: 3, 5 or 10 seconds from the capture box.

Hyper+Space; T in the capture box

Pin a capture

Float the last capture over every window; scroll zooms it.

Type its name in Hyper+Space

Screen recordingHyper+R

Record a screen, an app or an area, with sound and clicks shown; pause and resume.

Hyper+R; R in the capture box; Tools › Captures

Video editor

Trim, crop and speed up a recording, put it on a backdrop, and let it zoom in on your clicks and follow the pointer; each zoom moved, stretched and set on the timeline. Export MP4 (H.264 or HEVC) or GIF, faster than real time.

Recording thumbnail; Edit video… in the Capture menus; Tools › Captures › History

Capture menu

Every capture, the recording and the capture tools in one menu-bar menu, each with its key; while recording it shows the time, with Stop and Pause.

Capture item in the menu bar (on for a new install) or top bar; Tools › Captures (Capture options)

Clean desktop

Leaves desktop icons out of captures and recordings without touching the desktop.

Tools › Captures (Capture options)

Resize

Resize a capture to a size or a percentage, aspect locked or not, or any picture from Finder; the result lands beside the original.

Capture editor › Image size; Finder right-click › Resize with Pilot

Ask AI about a capture

Send the capture, blurs kept, to the AI chat.

Capture editor and thumbnail

Capture history

Every capture and recording with its thumbnail, app, date and size; search it, filter by kind, edit, copy, show or trash one; an optional size cap, kept on the Mac.

Tools › Captures › History

Combine images

Pick two or more captures and join them side by side or stacked, with a gap, then mark up the result.

Tools › Captures › History

Capture a subject

Capture an area with its background removed, on the Mac: a person, a product, a logo.

Hyper+Space (Capture menu)

Pixel magnifier

A pixel grid beside the pointer while you pick, with the colour's hex and RGB; copy either. Pilot's one colour picker: pick a colour anywhere on screen.

Any capture; Pick a colour in Hyper+Space › Trigger and the Capture menu

Make a QR code

The text you copied, or what you type, as a QR code; copy it as a picture or save it with your captures.

Hyper+Space › Trigger; Hyper+Space › QR (a More rows extra, off by default)

Read a QR code

Reads a QR code in the picture you copied, an image file, or an area you drag on screen (Read QR on screen goes straight to the drag); copy its text or open its link. A copied image with a QR code shows Open link (web and mail links only) or Copy text on its clipboard row and preview, once you select it.

Hyper+Space › Trigger; Hyper+Space › QR; Hyper+Space › Capture and the Capture menu (Read QR on screen); Hyper + right-click an image; clipboard history

Pilot
Pilot→dragApplications

Drag Pilot to Applications. Then hold Hyper.

Install Pilot 1.4.2.

Free and open source. Needs macOS 27 or later on Apple silicon.

  1. 1DownloadDrag Pilot to Applications
  2. 2Open PilotClick Open when macOS asks, once
  3. 3Pick your Hyper keyAnd allow Accessibility
Details
  1. Download Pilot.dmg, open it and drag Pilot to Applications.
  2. Open Pilot. macOS asks once whether to open an app downloaded from the Internet: click Open.
  3. In Pilot's setup, pick your Hyper key and a set of keys (Easy, Complex or Scratch), and allow Accessibility. Hyper+Space opens the menu.

Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Updates install from inside Pilot.

Permissions and checking the download

  • Accessibility: Pilot needs it to see your keys and move windows; nothing works without it.
  • Full Disk Access for file search and your browsers' bookmarks and history in the menu, and System Events for sleep, restart and dark mode.
  • Local Network only for the Network extension's list of devices.
  • Microphone for dictation and an AI provider for the AI chat, both optional.
  • Input Monitoring only if Pilot asks, when you bind a mouse's media buttons.
  • Screen Recording when you first take a screenshot or recording, or turn on Menu bar › Other apps › Show exact menu bar items. macOS applies it after Pilot reopens: click Quit & Reopen.

Caps Lock as Hyper: Shift+Caps Lock still types capitals, and a quick tap sends Escape once you switch it on in General. Password fields are blind to every key tap on macOS, Pilot's included: your binds do not work while one has focus.

Updates keep the permissions you gave. Check the download against the .sha256 beside it on the Releases page: shasum -a 256 -c Pilot.dmg.sha256.
